blocks.content: Official images on Docker Hub are a curated set maintained and reviewed by Docker in partnership with the upstream project teams, and they are almost always the right starting point for a base image.

An official image is not just popular, it goes through an actual review process: Docker and the upstream maintainers (the Nginx team for the nginx image, the PostgreSQL team for postgres) collaborate on keeping the Dockerfile, security patches, and documentation current.

blocks.alt: Docker and upstream maintainers jointly review the image

blocks.content: Official images cover the software you would expect: nginx, postgres, node, python, redis, and hundreds more, all reachable with just the short name, no username or organization prefix required.

blocks.alt: The names you already recognize are usually official

blocks.content:
docker pull postgres:15   # official, no publisher prefix needed
docker pull bitnami/postgresql  # a specific publisher's alternative

blocks.content: Docker Hub content roughly falls into three trust tiers: official images (most reviewed), verified publisher images (a company's own account, vetted by Docker but maintained solely by that vendor), and everything else, ordinary community accounts with no formal review process at all.

blocks.alt: Three tiers, from most to least reviewed

blocks.content: 4. Why This Should Influence Your FROM Line
blocks.text: 4. Why This Should Influence Your FROM Line

blocks.content: Preferring official images as your base is not just convention, it has a real security payoff: official images get security patches promptly and predictably, and you inherit those patches automatically the next time you rebuild your own image on top of an updated base.

blocks.alt: An updated official base means your image gets patched too

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Official images are reviewed jointly by Docker and the upstream project, not just popular community uploads, prefer them as a default base.
Choosing a well-maintained base image is a real, ongoing security decision, not a one-time convenience choice.
